request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 10-year-old female with developmental delay, microcephaly, epilepsy, severe short stature, impaired speech, facial dysmorphism, congenital deafness, and skeletal abnormalities.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to our Genetic Department due to the above-listed conditions. She was diagnosed with bilateral hip dysplasia, mixed hearing loss, and right conductive hearing loss. A genome-wide array, CGH (Agilent Human Genome CGH Microarray 44K), was conducted which diagnosed a minimal/maximal deletion of 5.238 Mb and 5.374Mb at 8q22.2q22.3. The patient’s sleep electroencephalogram displayed epileptogenic activity during nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep. Cerebral MRI tests were normal, as was the screening for inborn errors of metabolism. The patient was discharged after following up on the diagnosis it was shown that the deletion was excluded in her mother's blood sample, and the father was not available for investigation. 
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Summary:
The patient was a 10-year-old girl born with several conditions, including microcephaly, epilepsy, severe short stature, impaired speech, facial dysmorphism, congenital deafness, and skeletal abnormalities. After following up on the diagnosis, it was shown that the patient was diagnosed with a minimal/maximal deletion of 5.238 Mb and 5.374Mb at 8q22.2q22.3, which was not present in the mother's blood sample. The patient was discharged after the genome-wide array, and other tests showed no issues, but follow-up evaluation is necessary.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is the 8q22.2q22.3 interstitial deletion, which is the underlying cause of the multiple congenital anomalies, developmental delay and epilepsy. The admission was to the genetics department for this work-up, and the array CGH established it.

In ICD-10-AM, chromosomal abnormalities not elsewhere classified are in Chapter XVII, Q90–Q99. A deletion of part of a chromosome is coded to Q93, "Monosomies and deletions from the autosomes, not elsewhere classified". Q93.5 covers other deletions of part of a chromosome, and Q93.8 covers other deletions from the autosomes. Q93 is the right category for an 8q interstitial deletion.

The individual manifestations (epilepsy, hearing loss, hip dysplasia, short stature) would be coded as additional diagnoses where they meet reporting criteria. The principal diagnosis is the chromosomal deletion.

CODE: Q93
